//: The SPA rewrite must NOT swallow /assets/. Vercel applies rewrites after
the filesystem check, so a request for a build artefact that no longer
exists — which is what a browser holding a cached index.html asks for
after a deploy — fell through to /index.html and came back 200 with
Content-Type: text/html. The browser then tried to parse HTML as a

That was invisible while the app shipped as a single bundle, because
index.html always referenced the one current hash. Code-splitting the
routes made every page a separate hashed chunk and turned it into a real
failure mode. Excluding /assets/ lets a stale chunk 404 honestly, which is
what the reload handler in main.tsx detects and recovers from.

headers.//: Content-hashed filenames, so they can never go stale — cache hard.
